title: From Surveys to Narratives: Rethinking Cultural Value Adaptation in LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring cultural distinctiveness (via a proposed C-DIST metric) and cross-cultural interference by evaluating single-culture adapted models on a suite of multicultural, multilingual offensiveness, hate speech, and toxicity classification tasks across 10 distinct linguistic-cultural settings.

Evaluating the extent to which baseline and instruction-tuned models default to Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic (WEIRD) norms, and testing whether adapting them with World Values Survey (WVS) and narrative data mitigates cultural homogenization.
